event.description: JOIN US FOR OUR ANNUAL FUNDRAISER BREAKFAST Preserving our Past, Funding our Future Date: October 1, 2026 Location: Trinity Presbyterian Church Fellowship Hall, 3115 Providence Road, Charlotte Event Start: 8:30am New this Year – 50/50 RAFFLE! event.title: Artist Talk with Andrew Leventis | Shadow Play: The Caravaggesque in My Approach to Painting
event.description: Artist Andrew Leventis will share images of his work and discuss the Caravaggistic influence on his contemporary painting practice. The talk will explore facets of compositions, theatrical staging, and subject matter through the inspirational lens of the Baroque masters. About the artist: North Carolina-based artist Andrew Leventis explores themes of domesticity, consumption, and the passage of time. Drawing on the tradition of still-life painting, his work transforms familiar everyday objects and spaces into meditations on intimacy, impermanence, and human experience. With a thoughtful and compassionate approach, Leventis considers the complexities of contemporary life and our relationship to the ordinary.

event.title: Artist Talk: Constellation CLT with Grace Stott
event.description: Through ceramics, painting, and collage, Charlotte-based ceramic artist Grace Stott explores her family’s heritage, motherhood, and the objects that fill our daily lives. Her work reflects her journey toward accepting herself as an imperfect person and finding joy at every opportunity. Stott attended the California Institute of the Arts and completed her degree at Tufts University in Massachusetts, specializing in painting. After returning to Charlotte, she became one of the founding collective members of Goodyear Arts, a multidisciplinary artist collective. She quickly built a community of admirers and fellow makers who were curious to see where her portals would take them. Stott joins Chief Curator and Curator of Contemporary Art Jen Sudul-Edwards, PhD, to discuss her Constellation CLT installation, as well her practice and process. 6 PM: Cash bar opens 6:30 PM: Artist talk

Having released three records to critical acclaim, they have grown a cult following in the South and beyond, their introspective lyricism and blistering guitar techniques making the band potent in the studio and on stage. Their 2025 album Believer was hailed in Bandcamp’s Best New Country list and earned them slots on SXSW, Hopscotch Fest’s main stage opening for Geese and My Morning Jacket, and PBS’ new original series, Shaped By Sound. Blue Cactus have toured throughout the US, developing a dedicated cult following. From intimate clubs to major festival stages, Blue Cactus is known for connecting deeply with audiences wherever they go. linktr.ee/bluecactus Ramona & the Holy Smokes Formed in 2022, Ramona and the Holy Smokes have seen their star rise in the region and beyond. The band–which includes Kyle Kilduff (electric guitar), Brooks Hefner (pedal steel), Jay Ouypron (bass), and Porter Bralley (drums)–had built a rapport playing together before joining Ramona, and in their time together have brought their talents to Ramona’s songs and song ideas, shaping and arranging these for a signature honky tonk sound. The band has performed regularly in the region, appearing at several Americana festivals including Red Wing Roots (2024), Rooster Walk (2025), and Bristol Rhythm & Roots (2025), and has opened for touring artists like Margo Cilker, Colby Acuff, Willi Carlisle, Redd Volkaert, Joshua Hedley, Donna the Buffalo, and Kashus Culpepper. linktr.ee/ramonaandtheholysmokes Anna Kimm Anna Kimm is a Charlotte-based singer-songwriter blending heartfelt storytelling with a hint of warm, melodic country charm. Her music pairs honest lyrics with dreamy Americana textures and a soulful edge. As she steps into a new era, Anna is evolving her sound into a more crossover country style, weaving together classic country roots, indie influences, and polished pop sensibilities to create something both timeless and fresh. https://linktr.ee/annaxxkimm

event.title: The Art of Reading: “The Glassmaker”
event.description: Tracy Chevalier’s “The Glassmaker” paints a vivid portrait of Orsola Rosso. Orsola is a young woman forbidden by tradition to work with glass who secretly hones her craft, creating delicate beads that sustain her family’s fortunes after her father’s death. Set against the glittering backdrop of Renaissance Venice and skipping across centuries, this sweeping novel follows Orsola and her family through war, plague, love, and loss as she leaves her indelible mark on a male-dominated art form. “I suspect it will take a long time for women to be accepted into the glass world. Hundreds of years.” –Maria Barovier Guided tour, Mint Museum Uptown: Craft + Design, and Modern + Contemporary galleries Mint Museum Randolph: European Art and Delhom galleries to see connections to our art through the lens of a glassmaker shaped by centuries of tradition, transformation, and the fragile beauty of enduring craft.
